agents.name: Duplicate Agent
agents.statement: The same invoice cannot be paid twice.
agents.mechanism: Every arriving invoice is matched against every invoice that vendor has ever sent — the portal, the shared mailbox, the one handed to someone at the site office. The channel is not a hiding place.
agents.lede: Duplicates are not a fraud problem. They are a filing problem that costs real money, and they survive because the second copy usually arrives through a different door than the first.
checks: Invoice number against every prior invoice from the same vendor, not just the current period
Same amount, same date, same PO — the near-match that a changed invoice number is meant to hide
The same document arriving on a second channel after it was already booked
Credit notes that reverse an invoice which was never actually paid
reads: Vendor invoices from every channel — portal, email, file drop, scanned paper
The full invoice history for that vendor
writes: A hold on the second copy, before it can enter a payment run
The matching earlier invoice, attached, so the reviewer can see why
An audit entry recording what matched and who released it
agents.ambiguity: A near-match is not a duplicate. Where the amount and date align but the invoice number does not, the entry is held and both documents are put side by side for a person to decide — it is not silently released, and it is not silently blocked.

agents.name: Pricing Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is paid above the rate that was agreed.
agents.mechanism: Every line is checked against the contract and the PO it belongs to. A variance does not get approved quietly — it stops, and it names the buyer who owns the contract.
agents.lede: This is the largest of the six leaks, and the most ordinary. The contract says one number, the invoice says another, and nobody opens the contract for a bill this size.
checks: Line rate against the contracted rate for that item, that vendor, that period
Rate against the PO, where a PO exists and the contract does not cover the item
Price escalations claimed against the escalation clause that permits them
Freight, handling and surcharges against what the contract actually allows to be added
reads: The vendor contract and its rate schedule
writes: A hold on the line, with the variance in both percentage and rupees
The contract clause the line was tested against
A note to the buyer who owns the contract
agents.ambiguity: Where no contract covers the item, the agent says so rather than passing the line. An uncovered rate is a different finding from an overcharge, and it is reported as its own thing — usually it means a contract expired and nobody renewed it.

agents.name: 3-way match Agent
agents.statement: Nothing is paid for that wasn't received.
agents.mechanism: PO, GRN and invoice have to agree on quantity, rate and item before the entry stands. All three, on every line, every time.
agents.lede: The invoice bills 82 MT. The gate received 78. Both facts are true, and they live in different systems, which is why the difference is usually found in a stock reconciliation months later.
checks: Invoiced quantity against goods actually received, line by line
Item and specification, not just the total — a substituted grade at the contracted rate is still a variance
Partial deliveries billed as complete
Tolerances you define, applied consistently rather than at each approver's discretion
reads: Goods receipt notes from the plant or warehouse system
writes: A short-receipt finding with the quantity gap priced
The GRN reference the invoice was tested against
A hold until the gap is explained or the invoice is revised
agents.ambiguity: Where the GRN has not arrived yet, the invoice is not failed — it is parked as awaiting receipt, with the age of the wait visible. A missing GRN and a short receipt are different problems and are never merged into one.

agents.name: GST Agent
agents.statement: Input credit is never claimed before the vendor has earned it.
agents.mechanism: The vendor's filing status is checked at the point of entry, not discovered at the annual return when the credit has already been taken and spent.
agents.lede: Input credit depends on someone else's compliance. If the vendor has not filed, the credit was never yours to take — and finding that out a year later means reversing it with interest.
checks: Vendor GSTIN active and valid on the invoice date
Filing status for the relevant period before the credit is claimed
Place of supply, and whether the tax charged is the tax that should have been charged
Invoice appearing in the vendor's outward supplies, matched against what was booked
writes: A hold on the credit claim, not on the payment, where the vendor has not filed
The period and status the decision was based on
A follow-up to the vendor to file
agents.ambiguity: Filing status changes. A credit held today may be claimable next month, so the hold is a queue rather than a rejection — the claim is re-tested as status updates, and released when it qualifies.

agents.name: TDS Agent
agents.statement: Tax is deducted at the right section and the right rate, on every payment.
agents.mechanism: Vendor type, threshold and section are resolved before the entry is posted — not corrected in a return two quarters later, and not paid out of your own pocket as interest.
agents.lede: Under-deducting is the expensive direction. The shortfall is recoverable from the vendor in theory and almost never in practice, so it becomes a cost plus interest.
checks: The correct section for the nature of the payment, not the one used last time
Rate against vendor status — PAN validity, and whether a lower-deduction certificate applies
Annual thresholds, including whether this payment is the one that crosses them
Cumulative deduction against the vendor for the year, so the crossing is caught on the day
reads: Vendor master, PAN status and any certificates on file
Payment nature and the invoice narration
writes: The section and rate applied, with the reason recorded
A correction where the entry was raised at the wrong rate
A flag when this payment crosses a threshold
agents.ambiguity: Where the nature of a payment is genuinely arguable between two sections, the agent applies the higher-deduction reading and flags it for review, rather than choosing the cheaper one and leaving you exposed.

agents.name: Discount Agent
agents.statement: An early-payment discount that was available is never left unclaimed.
agents.mechanism: Discount terms are read off the contract and the invoice, and the payment run is built to hit the date the discount actually requires.
agents.lede: This is the only one of the six that is not a leak so much as an unopened envelope. The money is offered, the terms are on the invoice, and the approval takes twelve days when the discount needed ten.
checks: Discount terms on the invoice against the terms in the contract, where they differ
The date the discount actually expires, counted from the right event
Whether the run is scheduled to land inside that window
The trade-off, where taking the discount conflicts with a payment date set for cash reasons
writes: A recommended payment date that captures the discount
The value of taking it against the value of holding cash
A record when a discount was consciously let go, and why
agents.ambiguity: Cash position beats a discount sometimes, and that is a treasury decision rather than an accounts one. The agent surfaces the number and the deadline; it does not move a payment date on its own.
